With \(D=(1,0)\), \(E=(2,0)\), and \(A=\left(\frac32,\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}\right)\),

\[
\vec{AD}=\left(-\frac12,-\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}\right),\qquad \vec{AE}=\left(\frac12,-\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}\right).
\]

Their lengths are both
\[
\sqrt{\frac14+\frac{27}{4}}=\sqrt7.
\]
The cross product magnitude is
\[
\left|\left(-\frac12\right)\left(-\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}\right)-\left(-\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}\right)\left(\frac12\right)\right|
=\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}.
\]
Thus
\[
\sin(\angle DAE)=\frac{\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}}{\sqrt7\cdot\sqrt7}
=\frac{3\sqrt3}{14}.
\]
So \(a=3\), \(b=3\), \(c=14\), and
\[
a+b+c=3+3+14=\boxed{20}.
\]
